title: Mato Grosso, Brazil
subtitle: The same patch of Amazon, before and after clearing

source.agency: NASA/GSFC/METI/ERSDAC/JAROS, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team

facts: Dense green vegetation gives way to pale fields in these satellite images of deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon, taken by NASA's Terra satellite. The river is the same river in both frames — that is how you know it is the same place.
journeyIntro: Two pictures of the same river. In the first, the land around it is closed forest. In the second, it has been cut into fields. Press T to hear the change happen.

hotspots.name: The river
hotspots.text: The same river bends through both pictures. In the forest it runs white with sediment; in the cleared land it is blue and straight-edged, because the shade has gone.

hotspots.name: Closed forest
hotspots.text: Closed canopy. Every pixel here is leaves, and the sound is dense and even, with almost no edges — a forest has very little visual contrast.

hotspots.name: The fields
hotspots.text: Pale rectangles of pasture and soy. The edges are what you hear: each field boundary is a bright line, and each one puts a small accent into the music.

timeMachine.caption: Terra / ASTER, the same coordinates. The left frame is closed forest; the right is the same land after clearing.
